solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Spicy food in pastry cases can lead to trouble (7)

indicatorNotes.cases: the pastry encases the other letters, holding them inside
indicatorNotes.lead to: the leading letter of 'trouble' is taken

blocks.note: a pie is a pastry dish
surface padding, dressing the spicy picture
taken as written
its first letter

annotation.surface: A warning that eating hot food in pastry could end badly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spicy food' looks like the whole definition, but only the adjective is needed. 'can lead to trouble' reads as a warning; split it into a word taken as written and a leading letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Picante is a Spanish-derived word for spicy or hot, as in picante sauce.

entries.clue: Equips with cutlery supply in an attractive manner (13)

indicatorNotes.supply: read as supple-ly, in a supple or bendy way, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters; 'with' joins the two words
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A caterer laying out knives and forks so the table looks nice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun or verb meaning provision, but here it is the adverb from supple: bendily. That rare reading is the trick of the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Picturesquely means in a way pretty enough to be a picture, so attractively.

entries.clue: Restrict dogs (7)

blocks.note: read as a noun, a dog is a cur, a mongrel
read as a verb, to dog someone is to follow them closely

annotation.surface: A command to keep the dogs under control.
annotation.walkthrough: 'dogs' does two jobs: as a noun it gives CUR, and as a verb (to dog someone is to tail them) it gives TAIL.
annotation.definitionFit: To curtail something is to cut it short or restrict it.

entries.clue: Innocent I buried in central part of church (5)

indicatorNotes.buried in: the I goes inside, covered by the other word

blocks.note: the nave is the main central body of a church
taken as written

annotation.surface: Someone innocent laid to rest in the middle of a church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'central part' suggests taking a middle letter, but it is a definition of NAVE.
annotation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and inexperienced, lacking worldly wisdom.

entries.clue: Demand from alimony claim? (8)

blocks.note: alimony is claimed by an ex, a former spouse
a legal action is a claim brought in court

annotation.surface: A divorced partner's demands for money.
annotation.walkthrough: An alimony claim is an ex's action, which spells EX ACTION; the question mark flags the loose reading of 'alimony' as EX.
annotation.definitionFit: An exaction is a demand, especially one for payment that is hard to refuse.

entries.clue: Shot out of bed close to dangerous temporary installations (3-3)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close, or end, of 'dangerous' is taken

blocks.note: a pop is a shot, as from a gun
someone out of bed is up
its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone leaping out of bed near some dangerous structures.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot out of bed' reads as one phrase for springing awake, but it is two separate pieces: a gunshot, then being awake.
annotation.definitionFit: Pop-ups are temporary shops, stalls or displays set up for a short time.

entries.clue: Supply weapons before war? Starmer possibly holding back (6)

indicatorNotes.holding: PM holds the other letters inside it

blocks.note: Keir Starmer is a British Prime Minister, a PM
the back is the rear

annotation.surface: Speculation that the Prime Minister is quietly rearming ahead of a war.
annotation.walkthrough: 'holding back' reads as one phrase for restraint, but 'holding' is the container and 'back' stands alone. The question mark flags the playful definition: arming before a war.
annotation.definitionFit: To prearm is to arm in advance, so to supply weapons before the fighting starts.

entries.clue: Trump is one citizen following Putin’s overture (9)

indicatorNotes.overture: an overture opens a piece, so it gives the opening letter of Putin
indicatorNotes.following: something following comes after, so the citizen is placed after Putin's letter

blocks.note: its first letter
a resident is a citizen of a place

annotation.surface: Donald Trump described as an ordinary citizen taking his lead from Putin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'following' puts RESIDENT after P.
annotation.definitionFit: Donald Trump is an example of a president, of the United States.

entries.clue: The Now Show (7)

blocks.note: a noun: this moment in time, as opposed to past or future
a verb: to display or put on view

annotation.surface: The Now Show is a long-running BBC radio comedy programme.
annotation.walkthrough: The three words read as one title, the BBC Radio 4 topical comedy show, but split after 'Now'.
annotation.definitionFit: Two plain synonyms: a noun for the current moment, and a verb for putting something on display.

entries.clue: Ate garlic, transforming body tissue (9)

indicatorNotes.transforming: the letters are changed into a new form

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Eating garlic as if it could change your body.
annotation.walkthrough: The letters of ATE GARLIC rearrange into CARTILAGE.
annotation.definitionFit: Cartilage is the firm, flexible connective tissue in joints, ears and nose.

entries.clue: Revise setter’s boring conclusion (5)

indicatorNotes.boring: ME bores into END, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a conclusion is an end
the setter refers to themself as ME; 'setter's' is setter is

annotation.surface: An editor asking the setter to rewrite a dull ending.
annotation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull, describing the conclusion, but it is the drilling kind: ME goes into END.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean correcting a text by editing it.

entries.clue: Area covered by detective with additional clause in contract, one who must deliver (8,5)

blocks.note: a DI is a detective inspector; the area covered is the DI's patch
a police officer's patch is the area they cover
a rider is a clause added to a contract or bill

annotation.surface: A detective's territory bound up in a contract with extra conditions.
annotation.walkthrough: The area covered by a detective is the DI's PATCH, so the possessive 'S' comes from the detective. 'with' simply joins the parts.
annotation.definitionFit: A dispatch rider carries messages or parcels, usually by motorbike, and must deliver them.

entries.clue: Wise to follow universal convention (5)

indicatorNotes.to follow: to follow is to come after, so the wise word is placed after the universal letter

blocks.note: U is the film certificate for universal viewing
sage means wise

annotation.surface: Advice that it is wise to go along with what everyone does.
annotation.walkthrough: 'universal convention' reads as one phrase, but 'universal' gives only U and 'convention' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Usage is established custom or practice, a convention.

entries.clue: Bother about current head’s tendency to be late (9)

indicatorNotes.about: turned about, so DRAT runs backwards

blocks.note: 'Bother!' and 'Drat!' are both mild curses
I is the symbol for electric current
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

annotation.surface: Complaining about how often the current headteacher turns up late.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bother about' looks like worry over something, but 'Bother' is the exclamation DRAT, turned about.
annotation.definitionFit: Tardiness is lateness, the habit of arriving late.

entries.clue: Emergence of insect from active colonies (8)

indicatorNotes.active: the letters are lively and move about

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Insects pouring out of busy colonies, as from an ant nest.
annotation.walkthrough: An uncommon word, but the fodder is right there: COLONIES rearranges into ECLOSION.
annotation.definitionFit: Eclosion is an insect's emergence from its pupa case or egg.

entries.clue: Surprisingly, it results in help for understanding opera? (9)

indicatorNotes.Surprisingly: the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: anagram indicator
anagram fodder, 9 letters; 'results' is used twice over, as fodder and as the link

annotation.surface: A remark that something unexpectedly makes opera easier to follow.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder is 'it results': the IT and RESULTS letters rearrange into SURTITLES, with 'in' joining to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Surtitles are translated words projected above the stage so the audience can follow an opera.

entries.clue: Collar robber that is hiding (6)

indicatorNotes.hiding: the phrase conceals the answer within its letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words, starting after the first three letters of 'robber' and stopping before the final letter of 'that'

annotation.surface: A police instruction to collar a thief who is in hiding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Collar' looks like a verb for arrest, fitting the robber, but it is the noun: a bertha.
annotation.definitionFit: A bertha is a wide, deep collar, often of lace, on a woman's dress.

entries.clue: On reflection, somewhat wicked method to catch animals (4,4)

indicatorNotes.On reflection: a reflection is mirrored, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: somewhat is partly, in part
wicked means evil

annotation.surface: Musing that a way of catching animals seems a little cruel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' tempts a solver to hunt for a hidden word, but it simply gives PART.
annotation.definitionFit: A live trap catches an animal without harming it, a humane method of capture.

entries.clue: Middle Easterner from Bahrain regularly after narcotic leaves (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: every other letter of 'Bahrain' is taken
indicatorNotes.after: the Bahrain letters come after QAT

blocks.note: qat (khat) is a plant whose leaves are chewed as a stimulant drug
its 2nd, 4th and 6th letters

annotation.surface: A traveller from Bahrain after the narcotic has been left behind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like departs, but QAT is the name of the leaves themselves. 'narcotic leaves' is one definition of QAT.
annotation.definitionFit: A Qatari is a person from Qatar, a Gulf state in the Middle East.

entries.clue: Hospital stopping heart is relatively stupid (7)

indicatorNotes.stopping: H stops up the other word, plugging a gap in it

blocks.note: ticker is slang for the heart
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

annotation.surface: A remark that a hospital letting a heart stop is rather foolish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'relatively' signals a comparative: THICKER is more stupid.
annotation.definitionFit: Thick means stupid, so thicker is more stupid.

entries.clue: Famous husband will run India with Conservative (8)

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
'he is to go' means he will go
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

annotation.surface: A notable husband who will lead India alongside a Conservative.
annotation.walkthrough: 'will run' reads as one verb, but 'will' is IS TO and 'run' is just R.
annotation.definitionFit: Historic means famous or important in history.

entries.clue: Outrageously sexy rector with beer belly, perhaps going topless (7)

indicatorNotes.going topless: the top letter of PAUNCHY is removed

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for rector
a beer belly makes someone PAUNCHY; without its top P it is AUNCHY

annotation.surface: A rector with a beer gut taking his top off, which is outrageously sexy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outrageously' looks like an anagram signal, but it is part of the definition. In a down clue the top letter is the first.
annotation.definitionFit: Raunchy means sexually explicit or earthy, so sexy.

entries.clue: Cane puzzle with a third missing (6)

indicatorNotes.with a third missing: BAMBOOZLE has nine letters; the final three, a third of it, are dropped

blocks.note: to puzzle someone is to bamboozle them, a nine-letter word; drop its last three letters, Z, L and E

annotation.surface: A cane toy or puzzle with one of its three sections lost.
annotation.walkthrough: BAMBOOZLE has nine letters, so a third is three: drop the last three.
annotation.definitionFit: Bamboo is a woody grass whose hollow stems are used as canes.

entries.clue: Knock out European chasing bronze approximately 1600 metres back (9)

indicatorNotes.chasing: E runs next to TAN in the string, like a pursuer
indicatorNotes.back: the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a tan is a bronze colour on the skin
1 MILE is about 1,609 metres, with 1 read as I

annotation.surface: An athlete from Europe, trailing in bronze position over a mile, being knocked out of the race.
annotation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the whole wordplay, not just the mile. The digit 1 becomes the letter I, a common setter's trick.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from sport: both mean removing a competitor from a contest.

entries.clue: More conservative Britpop band covering Bowie at last (5)

indicatorNotes.covering: BLUR covers the letter, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.at last: the letter that comes at last, at the very end, of Bowie's name

blocks.note: Blur were a leading 1990s Britpop band
its last letter

annotation.surface: A 1990s band doing a David Bowie cover in a rather more conservative style.
annotation.walkthrough: 'covering' looks like a band's cover version of a song, but it means BLUR wraps round E. Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative party, so bluer means more conservative.
annotation.definitionFit: Blue is the Conservative party colour, so bluer means more Tory.

entries.clue: Easily close growing business losing millions (2,3)

indicatorNotes.losing: the M for millions is lost

blocks.note: close by is nearby
a farm is a business that grows crops; without M it is FAR
M is the abbreviation for millions; it is the letter lost

annotation.surface: A fast-growing company closing down easily after losing millions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'growing business' reads like an expanding company, but it is one that grows things: a FARM.
annotation.definitionFit: By far means easily or by a wide margin, as in easily the best.

entries.clue: Peasant couple start to live (5)

blocks.note: to yoke is to couple, join together
its first letter

annotation.surface: A peasant pair setting up home together.
annotation.walkthrough: 'couple' reads as a pair of people, but it is the verb: to YOKE.
annotation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated country person, a peasant.

entries.clue: Festival established for Spooner is outrageous (9)

indicatorNotes.for Spooner: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: a fair is a festival
established means based, founded
swap the F and B sounds: BEAR FACED

annotation.surface: A festival that has been set up in an outrageous way.
annotation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of FAIR BASED gives BARE FACED.
annotation.definitionFit: Barefaced means shameless and undisguised, as in a barefaced lie: outrageous.

entries.clue: Work of art liberated Celt, mostly (6)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of each word is kept: its last letter is dropped

blocks.note: liberated is FREE; without its last letter, FRE
a Scot is a Celt; without its last letter, SCO

annotation.surface: A painting of a Celt who has been largely set free.
annotation.walkthrough: 'mostly' applies to both FREE and SCOT, not just the Celt.
annotation.definitionFit: A fresco is a painting made on wet plaster, a work of art.

entries.clue: An enthralling cultured raver? (7)

indicatorNotes.enthralling: PER holds ARTY captive inside it

blocks.note: 'an' means per, as in five pounds an hour
arty means interested in the arts, cultured

annotation.surface: A cultivated person enjoying a rave.
annotation.walkthrough: 'An' is the small word most easily overlooked; here it means PER. 'enthralling' looks like praise, but it holds ARTY captive.
annotation.definitionFit: A partyer is someone who goes to parties, a raver.
